title: DoorDash pays workers to load Dot robots with orders
excerpt: DoorDash is using gig workers to load orders into its Dot delivery robots, highlighting limitations in autonomous delivery technology.
content_html:
DoorDash is paying people to load its delivery robots. It points to a shortcoming of automation

By Alex Bitter

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

DoorDash's delivery robots need a hand.

Some workers in areas where DoorDash is using its Dot delivery robot are receiving offers through the DoorDash app to load them up. While the vehicles can navigate miles to delivery destinations, it's the few feet between a restaurant's pickup counter and the curb outside where delivery workers intervene.

Devena Bybee, a DoorDash gig worker in Mesa, Arizona, said that she received one such offer in early July. The company is using the robots to make deliveries in the Phoenix area.

Bybee drove about two miles to a restaurant, picked up an order, and placed it in the Dot robot as it waited in the parking lot, she said. She took photos of each step to document the process, and the gig took five minutes, she said. DoorDash paid her about $5.

Bybee was surprised that Doordash asked her to complete the task instead of a restaurant worker who was already on-site. "I just don't see how it's efficient," she said.

On Facebook groups for DoorDash workers, some posts show screenshots of similar gig offers over the past month.

"I would never do a five-dollar order, but I was really curious about this and I was super close to the restaurant," reads one July 6 post showing a robot-loading gig at a Burger King in Scottsdale, Arizona. The poster did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

"Dashers are essential to our platform and will continue completing the majority of deliveries even as our autonomous technology scales," a DoorDash spokesperson said.

"This limited pilot is designed to support merchants during busy periods, while creating more earning opportunities for Dashers outside of traditional deliveries," the spokesperson added.

A sticking point for automation

The loading gigs are the latest example of DoorDash workers stepping in when autonomous vehicles can't complete a job on their own.

Some workers received offers from DoorDash to close open doors on Waymo's self-driving cars in Atlanta, Business Insider reported in February. Waymo plans to add a self-closing function to its vehicles in the future, the companies said at the time.

Dot, which DoorDash unveiled in September, is roughly the size of a baby stroller and can hold up to 30 pounds of cargo. The robot can navigate both roads and sidewalks to travel between restaurants and customers' homes.

Handing off orders from restaurants to robots is a challenge to the rollout of autonomous deliveries, DoorDash CEO Tony Xu said last August, shortly before the company debuted Dot.

While loading an order only takes a few minutes, restaurants that receive lots of robot-delivered orders might have an incentive to outsource the task to DoorDash, said Robert Bruno, a professor of labor and employment relations at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

DoorDash's gig workers, who are independent contractors, don't receive the same employee benefits and hourly pay rate that most restaurant workers do, Bruno said.

"Multiplied over the course of a year or more, there's probably a real savings," he said.

Bybee, the DoorDash worker in Arizona, said that the loading gig left her more confident that humans are still needed for delivery work.

"There's only so much right now that the robots can do," she said.

作者：Alex Bitter 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

DoorDash 的送货机器人需要有人帮忙。

DoorDash 使用 Dot 送货机器人的地区的一些工作人员正在通过 DoorDash 应用程序接收报价以装载货物。 虽然车辆可以行驶数英里到达送货目的地，但餐厅的取货柜台和送货人员干预的外面路边之间只有几英尺。

亚利桑那州梅萨市 DoorDash 的一名零工 Devena Bybee 表示，她在 7 月初就收到了一份这样的工作邀请。 该公司正在使用机器人在凤凰城地区送货。

她说，Bybee 开车大约两英里到一家餐馆，拿起一份订单，然后将其放入在停车场等待的 Dot 机器人中。 她说，她拍摄了每个步骤的照片来记录整个过程，演出花了五分钟。 DoorDash 付给她大约 5 美元。

Bybee 很惊讶 Doordash 要求她来完成这项任务，而不是已经在现场的餐厅工作人员。 “我只是不明白它的效率如何，”她说。

在 DoorDash 员工的 Facebook 群组中，一些帖子显示了过去一个月类似工作机会的屏幕截图。

“我永远不会点五美元的订单，但我对此真的很好奇，而且我离餐厅非常近，”7 月 6 日的一篇帖子中写道，该帖子展示了亚利桑那州斯科茨代尔一家汉堡王的机器人装载工作。 该发帖者没有立即回应置评请求。

DoorDash 发言人表示：“Dashers 对我们的平台至关重要，即使我们的自主技术规模不断扩大，Dashers 仍将继续完成大部分交付。”

该发言人补充道：“这一有限的试点项目旨在为繁忙时期的商家提供支持，同时为 Dasher 在传统配送之外创造更多盈利机会。”

自动化的症结所在

当自动驾驶车辆无法自行完成工作时，装载工作是 DoorDash 工作人员介入的最新例子。

据 Business Insider 今年 2 月报道，一些员工收到了 DoorDash 的邀请，要求关闭亚特兰大 Waymo 自动驾驶汽车的大门。 两家公司当时表示，Waymo 计划未来为其车辆添加自动关闭功能。

DoorDash 在 9 月份推出的 Dot 大约有婴儿车大小，最多可容纳 30 磅的货物。 该机器人可以在道路和人行道上行驶，在餐厅和顾客家之间移动。

去年 8 月，DoorDash 首席执行官托尼·徐 (Tony Xu) 在公司推出 Dot 前不久表示，将订单从餐厅​​交给机器人是推出自动送货的一个挑战。

伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳-香槟分校劳动和雇佣关系教授罗伯特·布鲁诺 (Robert Bruno) 表示，虽然加载订单只需要几分钟，但收到大量机器人配送订单的餐厅可能有动力将任务外包给 DoorDash。

布鲁诺说，DoorDash 的零工工人是独立承包商，他们无法获得与大多数餐厅工人相同的员工福利和时薪。

“经过一年或更长时间的积累，可能会真正节省成本，”他说。

亚利桑那州 DoorDash 的工人 Bybee 表示，装载工作让她更加确信送货工作仍然需要人类。

“现在机器人能做的事情就这么多了，”她说。
